status: Retrospective analysis of previously scored public slates. These comparison definitions are fixed before calculating the new results.
population: Original fixed XGBoost voter, Gain anchor, half-width slate, 10-task/30-fold and 6-task/16-fold panels, preserve singleton no-action folds. Use XGBoost and standardized logistic receiving learners with their original corresponding anchor, one-candidate guard, fallbacks and outer metrics.
strict_gain: Sum the original distinct within-anchor feature ranks of every retained candidate. The slate always contains the prefix of the common width, which alone minimizes that sum. Check the support identity and record how many candidates tie. Separately reconstruct the original XGBoost fitting model and its average training split gain (importance_type=gain), sum its values over each retained set with math.fsum, and check for exact ties at the highest raw-gain mass. Record any rank discrepancy and halt instead of imputing raw gains.
primary_shortlist: For m eligible candidate supports retain the first ceil(m/2) in the original Gain rank-sum order, count equals by sorted column IDs as in the recorded selector. This forms a new coarse Gain selector. Also report strict best-rank, strict raw-gain mass, first ceil(m/4), first ceil(3m/4) and the entire slate as prespecified sensitivity endpoints. Distinct shortlist fractions are fixed regardless of realized scores. For m=0 keep the anchor.
factorial: Within each Gain shortlist compare all four policies: exact uniform across all shortlisted candidates; highest empty-context one-panel point margin; maximum integer min vote with uniform among all top-vote ties; and maximum integer min vote with point breaking its ties. Residual exact point ties favor the original Gain order. Full-slate versions recover the published no-vote and vote-primary policies. Singletons are decided without masking. Score lotteries exactly using each possible real guarded return.
estimates: For each learner and panel compare adding vote at fixed uniform or fixed point, matched by fold. Primary metric is task-equally weighted fraction of anchor columns saved under the original tolerances. Also report breach rate and mean retained fraction, outer AUC/accuracy, paired descriptive 95% percentile intervals resampling complete tasks 30000 times (seed 33119), changes in distributions of nominees/returned supports, task contributions, and bounds based only on guarded supports. No pooled inferential test over folds or claims of population equivalence.
cost: On original fitting/proposal inputs, time only the nomination after the common initial fit/anchor. For the primary top-half shortlist measure zero/point/vote/point plus vote strategies with fresh prediction caches. A single shortlisted candidate requires zero evaluations. The uniform vote variant must preserve all ties, pruning only proven losers; the point version can pre-order by point and abort when an integer tie cannot beat the incumbent. Report unique predictor masks, fixed downstream guard fit budget, local wall time and implementation convention. Do not interpret CPU-independent speed from single timings. Archive selected support distributions and costs before the retrospective join to already available outer scores.
